correctness.rationale: For the three real unit Mercedes vectors with Euclidean signal and phaseless measurement metrics, the cited published orthogonal-pair reduction reduces exact global inverse-Lipschitz optimization to x⊥y. Writing lengths r,s, squared measurement difference equals 3(r²+s²)/2−rs L(2θ), with L(t)=Σ_{k=0}²|sin(t+2πk/3)|≤2 by an exact one-sector trigonometric maximization. Hence D²≥(r²+s²)/2+(r−s)², giving d±≤√2 D. Equal-norm orthogonal x=(1,1)/√2 and y=(−1,1)/√2 have d±=√2 and D=1. Thus C=√2 is mathematically correct, including exact normalization and sharpness. However a prior published general harmonic-frame theorem already implies exactly this special case.
